sections.title: Clinical Definition & Spectrum
sections.content: Acute Coronary Syndrome (ACS) represents a spectrum of clinical conditions ranging from unstable angina (UA) to non–ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) and ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). It is characterized by a sudden reduction in blood flow to the heart, typically due to plaque rupture or erosion and subsequent thrombus formation.

branches: Plaque Rupture/Erosion: Most common; exposes prothrombotic core
Thrombosis: Platelet aggregation and fibrin mesh formation
Inflammation: Cytokine-mediated weakening of the fibrous cap
Coronary Vasospasm: Prinzmetal angina or cocaine-induced
Supply-Demand Mismatch: Type 2 MI (Tachycardia, Anemia, Sepsis)
Spontaneous Coronary Artery Dissection (SCAD): Non-atherosclerotic tear

sections.title: Emergency RED FLAGS
content: New onset S3 gallop or pulmonary rales (Acute Heart Failure)
New systolic murmur (Papillary Muscle Rupture or VSD)
Persistent hypotension (Cardiogenic Shock)
Dynamic ST-segment changes despite therapy
Ventricular Tachycardia or Fibrillation
Chest pain refractory to nitrates

sections.title: Differential Diagnosis: Not All Chest Pain is ACS

branches: GI: GERD, Esophageal Spasm, Boerhaave Syndrome

content.explanation: M: Morphine (if pain refractory), O: Oxygen (if Sat <90%), N: Nitrates (Vasodilation), A: Aspirin (325mg chewable), B: Beta-blockers (if no HF), A: ACE Inhibitors, S: Statins (High-intensity), H: Heparin/Anticoagulation.

sections.title: Step-by-Step STEMI Protocol
content: Step 1: Immediate 12-Lead ECG (within 10 minutes of arrival)
Step 2: Loading doses of ASA (325mg) and P2Y12 inhibitor (e.g., Ticagrelor 180mg)
Step 3: Assess for Primary PCI (Door-to-balloon time < 90 mins)
Step 4: If PCI not available within 120 mins, consider Fibrinolytics (Door-to-needle < 30 mins)
Step 5: Anticoagulation (UFH or Bivalirudin)
Step 6: Post-procedure Statins and Beta-blockers

sections.title: The Ophthalmic Connection
content: Hollenhorst Plaques: Cholesterol emboli seen on fundoscopy suggest carotid or aortic atherosclerosis, risk markers for future ACS.
Hypertensive Retinopathy: Grades III-IV indicate severe systemic end-organ damage and higher risk for MI.
Perioperative Management: Ophthalmic surgery is low risk, but ACS in the last 6 months requires cardiology clearance.
Antiplatelet Strategy: DAPT (Aspirin + P2Y12) should generally not be stopped for intravitreal injections or cataract surgery.

branches: LV Free Wall Rupture: Leads to Cardiac Tamponade (Days 3-5)
Papillary Muscle Rupture: Acute Mitral Regurgitation & Pulmonary Edema
Ventricular Septal Defect (VSD): New harsh systolic murmur; L-to-R shunt
Dressler Syndrome: Post-MI Pericarditis (Weeks later; autoimmune)
Ventricular Aneurysm: Persistent ST elevation weeks after MI

rows: PLATO Trial: Superior to Clopidogrel in ACS
PROVE IT-TIMI 22: High dose better post-ACS

sections.title: Key Clinical Pearls
content: High-Sensitivity Troponins (hs-cTn): Can rule out MI in 1-3 hours if initial levels are low and repeat levels are stable.
Type 2 Myocardial Infarction: Ischemia due to supply-demand mismatch (e.g., severe anemia) rather than plaque rupture; treatment involves correcting the underlying cause.
Dual Antiplatelet Therapy (DAPT) Duration: Standard is 12 months post-PCI, but can be shortened to 1-6 months for high-bleeding risk patients.
Cocaine-Induced MI: Avoid non-selective beta-blockers due to risk of unopposed alpha-adrenergic stimulation/vasospasm.
The 'Widow Maker': Proximal LAD occlusion, leading to massive anterior wall infarction and high mortality.
